CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE PRADEEP SINGH YERUR  ORAL ORDER

This petition is filed by the accused Nos.1 and 2 challenging the order passed by the Special Judge in Spl.C.C.No.73/2016 dated 24.11.2021 whereby, the application filed by the accused Nos.1 and 2 i.e.,
petitioners herein under Section 216 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 came to be rejected,
wherein, the accused Nos.1 and 2 had sought for alteration of the charges.
NC: 2024:KHC:38059 2.

It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the impugned order passed by the learned Special Judge was perverse, arbitrary, illegal and error apparent on the face of the record and hence, the same requires to be set aside and consequently, an application filed by the petitioners/accused to be allowed.

sentences.text: It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the internal accounting procedures and whether accused Nos.1 and 2 have caused any loss to the Bank would be in the better knowledge of the Chief Auditor of Bank who has conducted Internal Special Investigation and has provided the report.
Accordingly, question is whether loss of cause is attributable in any Staff, which has been answered by the Chief Auditor.
Therefore, it is conclusively proved that there was no loss caused by the accused Nos.1 and 2.
It is also contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that mortgaged property is intact and the question of loss does not arise.
It is probably only the case of recovery process, which is getting delayed.
4. It is contended by learned counsel that the provisions of Section 216 of Cr.P.C. contemplates alteration of charge which could be made by the Trial Court.

In the present NC: 2024:KHC:38059 case, there is no material to show any loss has been caused due to the acts of accused Nos.1 and 2 and charge has been framed against the present accused for the offences punishable under Sections 120(B) r/w Sections 409, 419, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC, 1860 and Sections 13(2) R/w Sections 13(1)(C)(d) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

5. It is also contended by learned counsel that charges framed by the learned Special Judge is erroneous on the basis of incorrect material statements for false accusations made by accused Nos.1 and 2, contrary to the Internal Audit Report.
Therefore, the charges framed and have to be altered.

Learned counsel for the petitioners before the Trial Court has pleaded to drop the charges for the offences punishable under Sections 420 467, and 468 of IPC, therefore, the application under Section 216 of Cr.P.C. came to be filed.
The said application was seriously opposed by the respondent-State on the ground that the said application is not maintainable.

On the ground that charges have been framed against accused persons, question of alteration of the charges does not arise and since, there is a invocation of Section 120-B of IPC all conspirators are held liable for the offences equally, and so also a case is made out NC: 2024:KHC:38059 against accused Nos.1 and 2 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of IPC and all other offences for the charges being framed.
6. It is vehemently contended by learned counsel for the respondents that no cogent material or reason has been placed on record to alter the charge already framed by the Court.

It is also contended by the learned counsel representing respondents that on the earlier occasion, application for discharge came to be filed by accused Nos.1 and 2, same has been rejected, pursuant to which evidence of the prosecution witnesses PW-1 to PW-17 is recalled.
After which the present application is filed, which prima facie goes to show that the application is filed only to protract and delayed the proceedings.

7. It is also vehemently contended by the learned counsel for respondents that the Trial Court has considered the submissions of the learned counsel perused the provision of law and not being satisfied with the contentions stated therein has rightly rejected the application, which does not call for interference at the hands of this Court.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the respondents.

The point that arises for consideration is:-
(i) whether petitioners have made out a ground to show any illegality, perversity or any error committed by Trial Court (Special Court)?
10. While passing the impugned order.
The facts are not in dispute with regard to the offences charged against the petitioner/accused Nos.1 and 2 as stated hereinabove.
It is also not disputed that accused Nos.1 and 2 had filed an application for discharge, which came to be rejected by the Trial Court.

Thereafter, evidence of the prosecution witness PW-1 to 2024 SCC OnLine SC 2283 (2020) 1 Karnataka Law General 819 NC: 2024:KHC:38059 PW-17 is adduced and thereafter, the present application is filed.

11. Vehement reliance is placed by the learned counsel for the respondents in the case of K. Ravi (supra), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court at paragraph Nos.10 and 11 has held as under.
"10.
Thus, the scope of interference and exercise of jurisdiction under Section 397 Cr.P.C. is extremely limited.

Apart from the fact that subsection 2 of Section 397 prohibits the Court from exercising the powers of Revision, even the powers under sub- section 1 thereof should be exercised very sparingly and only where the decision under challenge is grossly erroneous, or there is non-compliance of the provisions of law, or the finding recorded by the trial court is based on no evidence, or material evidence is ignored or judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or perversely by framing the charge.

The Court exercising Revisional Jurisdiction under Section 397 should be extremely circumspect in interfering with the order framing the charge,
and could not have interfered with the order passed by the Trial Court dismissing the application for modification of the charge under Section 216 Cr.P.C., which order otherwise would fall in the category of an interlocutory order.
11.

It is trite to say that Section 216 is an enabling provision which enables the court to alter or add to any charge at any time before judgment is pronounced, and if any alternation or addition to a charge is made, the court has to follow the procedure as contained therein.

Section 216 does not give any right to the accused to file a fresh application seeking NC: 2024:KHC:38059 his discharge after the charge is framed by the court, more particularly when his application seeking discharge under Section 227 has already been dismissed.
Unfortunately, such applications are being filed in the trial courts sometimes in ignorance of law and sometimes deliberately to delay the proceedings.

Once such applications though untenable are filed, the trial courts have no alternative but to decide them, and then again such orders would be Sri K R Sheshuprasad vs The Central Bureau Of Investigation on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106840164/
4 challenged before the higher courts, and the whole criminal trial would get derailed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Suffice it to say that such practice is highly deplorable, and if followed, should be dealt with sternly by the courts."
12. On careful perusal of the provisions of Section 216 of the Cr.P.C. reads as under:
216. Court may alter charge.-(1) Any Court may alter or add to any charge at any time before judgment is pronounced.
(2) Every such alteration or addition shall be read and explained to the accused.

(3) If the alteration or addition to a charge is such that proceeding immediately with the trial is not likely, in the opinion of the Court to prejudice the accused in his defence or the prosecutor in the conduct of the case the Court may, in its discretion, after such alteration or addition has been made,
proceed with the trial as if the altered or added charge had been the original charge.

(4) If the alteration or addition is such that proceeding immediately with the trial is likely, in the opinion of the Court to prejudice the accused or the prosecutor as aforesaid, the Court may either direct a new trial or adjourn the trial for such period as may be necessary.

NC: 2024:KHC:38059 (5) If the offence stated in the altered or added charge is one for the prosecution of which previous sanction is necessary, the case shall not be proceeded with until such sanction is obtained, unless sanction had been already obtained for a prosecution on the same facts as those on which the altered or added charge is founded.

13. Two contentions on legal issues arise in view of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court, firstly, whether the application filed under Section 216 of Cr.P.C. to be considered by the Trial Court.
Pursuance to an application filed for discharge being rejected at the instance of the same accused.
Secondly, whether the orders passed under Section 216 of Cr.P.C. fall within the category of an interlocutory order.
Thereby, falling within the category of Section 397 (2) of Cr.P.C., which pass filing of revision petition on any order that is passed on interlocutory orders.
As held by the Hon'ble Apex Court Section 216 of Cr.P.C. is an enabling provision which enables to Court alter or add to any charge at any time before judgment is pronounced.

14. The Hon'ble Apex Court is further gone on to hold that Section 216 of Cr.P.C. does not give the right to the accused to file a fresh application seeking his discharge after - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:38059 the charges were framed by the Court.
Admittedly, charges were framed, an application was filed seeking discharge, which came to be dismissed and thereafter, the present application under Section 216 of Cr.P.C. is filed.

Therefore, in the present case on hand, the charge is already been framed by the Court, it was open for the petitioners to have file an application at the relevant time for alteration of the charge, if he had not filed his application for discharge.

Pursuant Sri K R Sheshuprasad vs The Central Bureau Of Investigation on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106840164/
5 to an application filed for discharge being rejected, seeking to file an application to alter the charge thereafter under Section 216 of Cr.P.C., in my humble opinion would not give the right to the petitioners/accused to file such an application for alteration of charge, which is also clearly held by the Hon'ble Apex Court.

sentences.text: This is apparently clear that the said application is filed only for the purpose of protracting and dragging the proceedings and not with true intent to alter the charge framed by the Court.
15. It is also relevant to see that in the present case, prosecution has examined 17 witnesses and thereafter, this application is filed.

Under such circumstances, this Court does not find favour with the petitioner/accused having approached this Court on challenge made to the correctness and legality of - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:38059 the orders passed by the Trial Court.
It is also relevant to note that the Court which has framed the charge and rejected the discharge application cannot go back to alter the charge, which is not permissible.

Under such circumstances, I pass the following:
ORDER I.
The petition is dismissed.
